title: SRStack curated auction round dataset, version 1
description: A strict summary shape that preserves partial round observations. Schema validity is not source authentication, economic consistency, complete coverage, freshness, unit compatibility or projection admission. Keep supporting raw evidence separately; never store credentials or token inventories here. Synthetic datasets must identify themselves and are not live forecast defaults.

chain_id.description: Canonical decimal chain identity; real use requires an authenticated positive chain ID.

label.description: Arbitrary authenticated denomination identity, not a ticker assumed to mean USD. No built-in asset list.

decimals.description: All raw price fields share this exact base-10 scale.

curated_at.description: Curation time, not a substitute for a block-header timestamp or a freshness certificate.

rounds.description: Chronological comparable candidates, including explicit partial or no-sale records. Consumers check identities, chronology, gaps, generation and unit compatibility before selecting a projection cohort.

sources.description: Optional public source/evidence identities. Raw logs, headers, receipts, coverage and conflicts belong in referenced supporting evidence, not a token inventory.

integerString.description: Nonnegative integer as a canonical decimal string. Never convert through binary float; unknown is not zero.

utcDateTime.description: ISO 8601 UTC with Z suffix. Enable date-time format checking to reject invalid calendar dates; schema implementations may otherwise treat format as annotation.

references.description: Public source IDs or evidence locations. Consumers resolve references and verify their claim-specific scope; an empty array provides no supporting evidence.

identity.description: Public original identity or durable evidence location, never a credential-bearing URL.

ts.description: Actual containing block's node-header Unix timestamp in integer seconds. Never block number times average block time, retrieval time or a fabricated timestamp.

nullableSaleAnchor.description: Null means unavailable anchor or no observed sale, as distinguished in notes/evidence. Keep incomplete anchors in supporting evidence rather than inventing a missing block or timestamp.

head_block.description: Observation/reconstruction horizon, not proof every intervening block was searched.

head_timestamp.description: Pinned head block's Unix timestamp in integer seconds. Node-header evidence is required for time/freshness assertions.

head_block_hash.description: Pin the hash here or in referenced evidence for canonicality and freshness checks.

coverage.description: Claim-specific supplied history coverage. Complete is a curator's evidenced assertion, not a schema or receipt-verification certificate.

timestamp_basis.description: Unknown timestamps cannot support timed projection admission. Synthetic fixtures may model header-shaped inputs only when explicitly marked synthetic.

sellout_basis.description: Evidence-backed explanation of positive capacity exhausted by purchases, capacity/settings changes and reopening checks. Presence alone does not authenticate sellout.

generation.description: Authenticated generation identity; day IDs may reset across generations.

day.description: Contract round/day identifier, not a UTC calendar date. Composite identity includes dataset chain/family plus generation/contract/day.

scheduled_window.description: Effective scheduled interval in Unix seconds, normally [start,end). A candidate schedule is not promised inventory or an executable fill; missing effective timing stays null.

start_price_raw.description: Historical policy opening in dataset price units; not the expected next transaction price.

last_sale_price_raw.description: Last observed executed unit price. It is a qualified exhausted close only with complete ordered evidence and authenticated exhaustion; null is not zero.

floor_price_raw.description: Authenticated historical round floor, not a minimum observed sale or a promised future floor.

sold.description: Observed purchased quantity in the stated coverage, not the count of logs. A partial subtotal must remain marked partial.

round_cap.description: Authenticated effective round capacity, accounting for changes; zero allocation does not prove demand-driven sellout.

sellout.description: True requires evidence; false is an observed non-sellout, null is unknown. A supplied boolean alone is not proof.
